items.title: Albert "June" Gardner Interview, 1996-04-17
items.q: I was in the wash of Red with him. ... Nance, the two new bozo. We would have six, seven drummers always would be together. We would just practice together.

ctx.x: You know what, a lot of guys who went on the road, and Earl King would do this to me, I'll be with him and he'll say, see that guy, he's a great saxophone player. Nobody knows what, because he was always, they left. They were always gone. Yeah. So we don't, for the cats who stayed, like Red Tyler, Red didn't go on the road a lot. He was on sessions, but we know him from his records he was on.

Well that's why one of the things I used to say, if we would all leave, we wouldn't have anybody say hello to when we come back. You know what I'm saying? Everybody was leaving in the 50s and early 60s, according to California and other places. And there's a lot of people that, somebody would be talking about musicians, they'd say, well I've never heard of him. They'd say, well he's been here all his life. He played. There's quite a few guys. Harry Nance, the drummer. Been everywhere twice, played with a lot of…
How important was the radio? Did you listen to radio a lot as a kid?
